title: fix(rest): POST /batch and the /meta engine reads answer from the request's environment kernel on a hosted runtime (#30218)
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-zhuang"} -->
Part of #30218 · follows #30011 (PR #30013) and #30192 (PR #30195)

_Requested by **Sam** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01GsBogozeZG5sdpAARrN7HP?thread=cmsg_01GsBogozeZG5sdpAARrN7HPYLaC4gZBht1y9TL9mMjrFz)_

The card carries no `Claim:` naming this branch, so this body declares `Part of`; the owning seat closes the card by hand once this lands. Nothing of the card's framework half is left open here: what remains is cloud's pin round and its hosted reading (see *Acceptance notes*).

Clause-②: no
Metadata-protocol: none

## 维护者速读

- 改了什么：`objectQLProvider`（数据引擎）改成按请求所属环境取内核里的引擎，和 #30013、#30195 的其它接口同一种做法；四个用到它的地方（`POST /batch`、对象状态、已发布读取、meta 读取门的「已停用包」判断）都改为传入按请求解析出的环境 id。
- 为什么改：托管运行时上这四处一直用宿主内核的引擎。批量写会在宿主引擎上开事务、用宿主引擎做更新和删除，而新建走环境自己的协议，一个请求用了两个内核。
- 风险与回滚：只动 `packages/rest`。单内核部署（没有 `kernel-manager`）仍读插件自己的内核，测试钉住不变。回滚即撤销本 PR。
- 先看：`packages/rest/src/rest-api-plugin.ts`（`environmentScopedProvider` 加了自身内核一腿）、`packages/rest/src/batch-routes.ts`（事务入口）、`packages/rest/src/rest-environment-scoped-providers.test.ts`（最后两个 describe）。
- 两分钟验证：`pnpm --filter @objectstack/rest exec vitest run src/rest-environment-scoped-providers.test.ts src/rest-api-plugin-slot-lookups.test.ts`，预期 121 个全绿。
- 需要你做的：无，席位落地。

## What changes

**The card's fix.** `objectQLProvider` in `packages/rest/src/rest-api-plugin.ts` is now `environmentScopedProvider('objectql', objectQLOnOwnKernel)`, typed `IObjectQLEngine`, with the same legs and the same rule as the seams #30013 and #30195 scoped: a request for environment A is answered by A's engine or by nothing, never by the host's.

- `environmentScopedProvider` takes an optional own-kernel leg. The environment leg is unchanged: acquire the environment's kernel through `kernelManager.getOrCreate`, read the slot with `getServiceAsync`, read a branded "never registered" as `undefined`, and re-raise anything else. Only the last leg is swapped.
- `objectQLOnOwnKernel` is the old provider body, unchanged: the factory-aware `kernel.getServiceAsync('objectql')` that absorbs only the branded rejection, and the `LiteKernel` sync leg. A single kernel, the reserved `platform` id and a request in no environment still take it.

**Every consumer asks for the request's environment.** Each passes the id `RestServer.resolveRequestEnvironmentId` answers (the scoped param, else the host's `kernel-resolver` for a hostname-routed request). The call sits inside the `wiredEngineOrLoud` thunk, so an unwired provider still costs nothing and a rejection still answers 503:

- `batch-routes.ts`, the transactional `POST /batch`. `BatchRouteHost` gains `resolveRequestEnvironmentId`.
- `meta-object-state-routes.ts`, `GET /meta/object/:name/state/:field`. `MetaObjectStateRouteHost` gains it.
- `meta-item-history-routes.ts`, the disabled-owner check of `GET /meta/:type/:name/published`. `MetaItemPublishedRouteHost` gains it.
- `rest-server.ts`, the meta read gate's `isItemOfDisabledPackage`.

`computeExecCtx` reaches the provider only when no environment kernel was bound, and it already passed the resolved id, so it is unchanged.

Changeset: `patch` for `@objectstack/rest`. `scripts/engine-double-contract.pinned.json` gains the two rows its `--write` records for the harness's new engine double.

## Why

On cloud's hosted runtime one `RestApiPlugin` sits on the host kernel in front of every environment kernel. `objectQLProvider` read the host kernel's `objectql` whatever id it was handed, and the unscoped mount handed it none. `computeExecCtx` already read the environment kernel's engine, so on a hosted request the execution context and the door's engine came from different kernels.

For `POST /batch` that meant three things:

- the transaction opened on the host's engine;
- update and delete ops went through the host's engine;
- create ops went to the environment's protocol, joined to the host's transaction.

The ablation readings below show exactly that.

## Tests

The new cases live in #30013's harness (`rest-environment-scoped-providers.test.ts`), as two new top-level `describe`s, per the shared-harness rule.

The harness uses real `ObjectKernel`s:

- A host with the real plugin, `kernel-manager` and `kernel-resolver` sits in front of the environment kernels. The host now carries an engine of its own.
- Every engine records which kernel's engine made each call, and which transaction a write joined.
- Each registry knows one object (`acct_ENV`) and disables one package (`pkg_ENV`). A door judged by another kernel's registry therefore answers differently on the wire too.
- The double's `update` and `delete` open with `assertEngineUpdateDispatch` / `assertEngineDeleteDispatch`.

**Hosted, scoped and hostname mounts, env A and env B:**

- `POST /batch` (one create, one update, one delete) answers 200. The calls are exactly these:
  1. the transaction opens on the target's engine;
  2. the create goes through the target's protocol, inside the target's transaction;
  3. update and delete run on the target's engine, inside that transaction.

  No call of any kind reaches the other environment's engine or the host's.
- `GET /meta/object/:name/state/:field` answers 200 for `acct_ENV`, judged by the target's registry only.
- `GET /meta/:type/:name/published` asks the target's registry whether the owner package is disabled, and answers its 404. Any other registry would have served the document.
- The meta read gate's `isItemOfDisabledPackage` asks the target's engine only.

**Hosted, both mounts:** an environment whose kernel carries no engine answers `POST /batch` with 501 `NOT_IMPLEMENTED`, and the host's engine is not asked.

**Single kernel (no `kernel-manager`), both mounts:** the same four doors are answered by the one kernel's engine, unchanged.

**`rest-api-plugin-slot-lookups.test.ts`:**

- The scope table marks `objectql` environment-scoped.
- It is asked of `env_1`'s kernel for `env_1`, and of the plugin's own kernel for no id and for `platform`.
- With no `kernel-manager`, every environment-scoped provider reads the plugin's own kernel for every id.

## Acceptance notes

- The four doors now each resolve the request's environment once more. #30013's review noted this pattern, and #30195 also followed it. The hostname resolver is cached, and `resolveExecCtx` is memoised per request.
- `isItemOfDisabledPackage` still hands the raw route id to `p.getMetaItem`. `p` is the protocol already resolved for the request, which is where its environment comes from, so this is unchanged here.
- **Not proven here:** cloud's pin round, and a hosted reading of `POST /api/v1/batch` on its local stack (the card's done-when, on cloud's side).

## Verification

Readings on `objectstack-ai/objectstack`, branch `claude/project-thread-k1cdp9`, branched from `f2a9007e`, in a cloud container. The head is `8bb0c277`. The two commits after `54c86871` add only the changeset (`a5cde52d`) and the ledger JSON (`8bb0c277`), with no source.

| | the two harness files (121 cases) |
|---|---|
| **this branch at `8bb0c277`** | **121 green** (also 121 green at `54c86871`) |
| **ablation 1**: `rest-api-plugin.ts`, `rest-server.ts`, `batch-routes.ts`, `meta-object-state-routes.ts`, `meta-item-history-routes.ts` restored to `f2a9007e`, tests kept | **20 red**: all 18 new hosted cases, plus two slot-table cases. The 8 single-kernel cases stayed green. |
| **ablation 2**: only the four consumer sites reverted to the raw route id (`() => this.objectQLProvider!(environmentId)`), provider kept | **9 red**: every hosted case on the hostname mount. The scoped mount stayed green, because there the raw param is the environment id. |

What ablation 1 showed for the batch:

- the transaction opened on `host`'s engine;
- the create went through env A's protocol, inside `host`'s transaction;
- update and delete ran on `host`'s engine;
- the engine-less environment answered 500 instead of 501.

The harness imports the plugin and server from `src/` by relative path, so neither ablation goes through a built `dist/`. Ablations ran on the `54c86871` tree. Before each run I checked the mutation on disk by marker counts, and after it I restored from `HEAD` (`git diff HEAD` empty).

- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/rest test`, under `os-verify-lock`:
  - Test Files 386 passed (386);
  - Tests 7298 passed | 332 skipped (7630);
  - exit 0.

The 2 NOT-MEASURED both exited 3, PREREQUISITE NOT MET in this container. CI runs both.

- `node scripts/check-plugin-teardown-shape.mjs --self-test`: the shallow clone cannot read its positive-control commit. The diff-reading `node scripts/check-plugin-teardown-shape.mjs` exited 0.
- `pnpm check:dual-build-cjs-loads`: no full workspace build here.

`pnpm check:engine-double-contract` first exited 1, because the harness's new pinned doubles were not yet in the ledger. Its `--write` recorded the two rows in `8bb0c277`, and after that it exited 0.

16 families beyond the derivation also ran green. Among them:
